scenarioStory.history: Roommate found the patient breathing rapidly and unusually thirsty this morning after two days of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Patient reports her insulin pump alarm has been going off intermittently over the past two days and she is unsure whether it has been delivering insulin correctly. She endorses excessive thirst and frequent urination over that time and has been unable to keep fluids down since yesterday evening.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 22-year-old female with known type 1 diabetes sitting upright, breathing deeply and rapidly, with a fruity odor to her breath and signs of dehydration. → BGL checked, fluids started: Point-of-care glucose confirms severe hyperglycemia. Crew obtains a 12-lead to screen for hyperkalemic changes or ischemia and initiates a weight-based normal saline bolus for dehydration. → Reassessed after fluid bolus: Serial reassessment after the fluid bolus shows improving perfusion, a clearing sensorium, and easing respiratory distress. Patient is packaged for transport.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Nausea, vomiting, and rapid breathing for the past day

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 22-year-old female with known type 1 diabetes sitting upright, breathing deeply and rapidly, with a fruity odor to her breath and signs of dehydration.

scenarioEvents.name: BGL checked, fluids started
scenarioEvents.description: Point-of-care glucose confirms severe hyperglycemia. Crew obtains a 12-lead to screen for hyperkalemic changes or ischemia and initiates a weight-based normal saline bolus for dehydration.
relatedChecklist: Obtain 12-lead EKG to screen for hyperkalemic changes or ischemia
Normal saline bolus 1,300 mL IV (65 kg × 20 mL/kg = 1,300 mL) infused at 1,000 mL/hr
Assess for dehydration: sunken eyes, dry mucous membranes, tachypnea, tachycardia
Reassess vital signs, mental status, and dehydration signs after fluid bolus

scenarioEvents.name: Reassessed after fluid bolus
scenarioEvents.description: Serial reassessment after the fluid bolus shows improving perfusion, a clearing sensorium, and easing respiratory distress. Patient is packaged for transport.
relatedChecklist: Transport to closest appropriate receiving facility

scenarioEvents.name: Fluids given without reassessment
scenarioEvents.description: The fluid bolus was infused but the crew did not reassess vital signs or mental status afterward. The patient's mental status is declining rather than improving, with a widening pulse pressure and irregular respirations concerning for cerebral edema.
relatedChecklist: Recognize declining mental status as possible cerebral edema; stop IV fluids and elevate head of bed
Reassess and manage airway as needed given declining mental status
